answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by locking emission rewards in a time-gated vault instead of paying instantly. New accounts must post a bond and complete peer-attested work before any nectar drips out, with the vault releasing value slowly over weeks. Every attestation goes into a quartz-clear record of who vouched for whom. Analysts scan it for correlated clusters — supposedly independent agents sharing the same sponsors — and slash the whole group at once. Sybils become a bad trade: a bond plus weeks of work per identity, for a payout that freezes when the graph exposes the swarm.
